data.title: Baozun Earnings Call Signals Growth, AI and Profit Upside
data.description:
Baozun Inc ((BZUN)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Baozun’s earnings call carried a predominantly positive tone, supported by 11% group revenue growth, stronger BBM performance and a sharp improvement in year-to-date operating profitability. Investors also heard about Gap’s momentum, BEC’s profit expansion, better working-capital efficiency and growing platform recognition, although quarterly losses, higher spending and ongoing investment remained concerns.

Revenue Growth Continued Across the Group

Baozun’s third-quarter group revenue rose 11% year over year to CNY 2.4 billion, with both business segments contributing to the increase. Revenue for the first nine months also grew 11%, reaching CNY 7.5 billion.

Year-to-Date Profitability Improved

For the first nine months of 2026, non-GAAP operating income reached CNY 42 million, compared with a CNY 72 million operating loss a year earlier. The improvement reflects stronger business performance and tighter operating discipline, despite a loss in the latest quarter.

BBM Growth Accelerated

Brand management revenue increased 32% year over year to CNY 524 million, accelerating from 22% growth in the previous quarter. BBM’s non-GAAP operating loss narrowed 27% to CNY 28 million, helped by Gap’s progress and greater operating leverage.

Gap Moves Closer to Breakeven

Gap’s operating loss improved by more than 50% year over year, marking a significant step toward profitability. Management credited the brand’s stronger sales performance and operating improvements for the progress.

Gap’s Omnichannel Sales Strengthened

Gap posted 15% omnichannel same-store sales growth in the quarter, driven by higher conversion and larger average transaction values. Offline comparable-store sales rose 18%, while noncomparable stores added 12%, producing 30% total offline scale growth.

Product Momentum Spanned Gap’s Categories

Women’s, men’s and kids divisions all delivered double-digit growth, with kids and baby leading the group. Management pointed to stronger seasonal assortments, improved fabrics, wider product ranges, better launch timing and more effective product storytelling.

Gap Expanded Customer Engagement

Gap added 430,000 followers during the year, taking its membership base to 35 million and generating 45 million online engagements. Several campaigns ranked first on Weibo’s star product influence list during their launch periods, highlighting stronger brand visibility.

Gap Accelerated Store Expansion

Gap opened 22 stores in the third quarter, its highest quarterly total to date, ending September with 187 locations. The pace reflects the company’s effort to extend the brand’s physical reach alongside its online business.

New Markets and Store Formats Added

Gap opened its first two Macau stores, entered Jiangxi and launched a travel-channel location at Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station. It also opened a 1,300-square-meter, two-level flagship in Guangzhou, while preparing for expansion into Hong Kong and other markets.

Gap Improved Inventory Efficiency

Gap’s inventory turnover days improved 26% year over year. Healthier in-season sell-through and better seasonal planning helped the brand manage stock more efficiently while supporting sales growth.

Hunter Broadened Its Brand Footprint

Hunter expanded its range through collaborations with TAGI and GANNI and introduced a lightweight summer outdoor collection. It entered Shenzhen, opened its first Thailand flagship at Bangkok’s ICONSIAM and ended the quarter with 28 stores.

BEC Product Sales Led Revenue Growth

BEC revenue rose 6% in the quarter and 7% in the first nine months. Product sales grew 26.3% to CNY 522 million, supported by new partnerships in emerging categories such as pets, health and nutrition.

BEC Profitability Expanded Sharply

BEC’s first-nine-month non-GAAP operating income climbed to CNY 108 million from CNY 23 million a year earlier. The result underscores the segment’s improving earnings contribution even as its services revenue remained flat in the quarter.

Platform Recognition Reinforced Baozun’s Position

Tmall certified Baozun for store operations across apparel, sports and outdoor, home and lifestyle, consumer electronics and automotive. The company was also named Tmall Fashion Awards’ Selected Service Provider of the Year for a second consecutive year and retained diamond service provider status on Douyin.

Double 11 and Partner Demand Were Encouraging

Management described the Double 11 finish as very strong and said Baozun outgrew the marketplaces year over year. Electronics, sports and fashion, and luxury were strong categories, while partner marketing budgets remained stable as net GMV grew, implying higher absolute spending.

AI Program Expanded Across Baozun

An AI pilot that began in Gap’s e-commerce operations has become a group-wide productivity program with a 15-month roadmap, milestones and cost targets. Applications include product listings, campaign planning, virtual design and data processing.

AI Could Lower Store Labor Costs

Management expects the AI roadmap to reduce store-operation labor costs by 25% to 30% by the end of 2027. The Gap pilot has already improved productivity at the individual-unit level, according to the company.

Profit Ambition for 2028 Was Raised

Baozun lifted its group-level 2028 non-GAAP operating profit target to CNY 700 million. Management said AI deployment and lean transformation should support changes in BEC’s margin structure during 2026 and 2027.

AI Dianxiaomi Is Being Customized

The third version of AI Dianxiaomi is being piloted with Baozun’s brand partners to improve online explanations of product information and promotional mechanisms. With about 500 partners, the company said deeper customization is needed for inventory, content creation and other complex omnichannel tasks.

Working Capital and Fulfillment Improved

Working-capital turnover improved to 123 days from 183 days a year earlier, while inventory turnover shortened to 126 days from 180 days. Fulfillment costs fell 9% to CNY 453 million, reflecting ongoing cost-optimization work.

Liquidity Remained Strong

As of September 30, 2026, Baozun held CNY 2.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments. The balance gives the company financial flexibility as it funds store expansion, technology projects and newer brands.

Share Repurchase Added Investor Support

Baozun announced authorization for a share repurchase program of up to USD 10 million over the following 12 months. Management said the move reflected confidence in the company’s strategy and long-term prospects.

Emerging Brands Remain a Strategic Focus

Baozun continues investing in emerging brands through positioning, category expansion, retail growth and balanced online-first development. Management said Gap’s established teams, systems and infrastructure could help newer brands absorb costs and shorten their ramp-up periods.

Quarterly Operating Loss Increased

Third-quarter non-GAAP operating loss widened to CNY 41 million from CNY 11 million a year earlier. Management attributed the result mainly to BEC seasonality and planned investment in emerging BBM brands.

BEC Services Revenue Was Flat

BEC services revenue remained unchanged at CNY 1.4 billion in the quarter despite overall BEC growth. The result shows that product sales, rather than core services, were the main source of momentum during the period.

E-Commerce Product Margins Declined

E-commerce product-sales gross margin fell to 12.1% from 13.1% a year earlier. Management linked the decline to category-mix changes while it reshaped the product-sales portfolio and prioritized earnings quality.

Sales and Marketing Costs Increased

Sales and marketing expenses rose by CNY 147 million to CNY 1 billion. BEC spending increased by CNY 98 million, mainly for creative content and campaigns on Douyin and RedNote, while BBM spending rose CNY 51 million because of store expansion and marketing.

Seasonality Weighed on the Third Quarter

Management described the third quarter as e-commerce’s lightest seasonal period, with the effect amplified because partners completed a large share of annual plans in the first half. BEC also faced weaker consumption sentiment during the quarter.

Young Brands Still Require Investment

Hunter, Sweaty Betty and other newer brands remain in an investment and expansion phase. Baozun is balancing store-opening costs and marketing spending, while retaining the flexibility to invest more when faster scaling opportunities emerge.

Guidance Points to a Stronger Growth Phase

Baozun expects Gap to reach CNY 2 billion in revenue and full-year breakeven in 2026, while opening more than 50 stores, including about 20 in the fourth quarter. For 2027, it is targeting 40 to 50 additional stores and continued double-digit sales growth, alongside a strong fourth-quarter finish.

Longer-Term Targets Rely on AI and Margin Gains

The company expects its AI roadmap to cut store-operation labor costs by 25% to 30% by the end of 2027. Management also expects BEC’s margin structure to begin transforming in 2026 and 2027, while reaffirming the three-year plan behind the raised CNY 700 million 2028 non-GAAP operating profit target.

Baozun’s call combined solid growth with a clearer path toward better profitability, led by Gap, BEC and efficiency programs. The higher profit target and AI ambitions strengthen the investment story, but investors will still watch quarterly losses, margin pressure and the cost of expanding newer brands.

data.title: Bilibili Earnings Call Signals Stronger Growth Ahead
data.description:
Bilibili ((BILI)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Bilibili’s latest earnings call carried a strongly positive tone, with record user engagement, improving profitability, double-digit advertising growth and continued progress in AI. Management also highlighted a stronger game pipeline and ample liquidity, while acknowledging pressure from weaker game revenue, cautious advertisers, higher AI-related research costs and a likely moderation in AI advertising growth.

Record User Engagement

Bilibili’s daily active users rose more than 5% year over year to 124 million, while monthly active users increased nearly 5% to 394 million. Average daily time spent climbed by nine minutes to 121 minutes, pushing total user time up 14% and exceeding two hours for the first time.

Revenue and Profit Expansion

Third-quarter revenue grew 8% year over year to RMB 8.3 billion, while gross profit increased 10% to RMB 3.1 billion. Gross margin widened to 37.3%, operating profit rose 32% to RMB 469 million, and adjusted operating profit advanced 17% to RMB 807 million.

Improved Profitability Metrics

Adjusted operating profit margin expanded to 9.7% from 9.0% a year earlier, showing stronger operating leverage. Adjusted net profit rose 5% to RMB 828 million with a 10% margin, while reported net profit increased 7% to RMB 504 million.

Broad-Based Content Watch-Time Growth

General entertainment watch time increased more than 35% year over year, supported by broad demand across the platform. Sports and parenting and early education content each grew 47%, AI-related knowledge viewing more than doubled, and AI tools helped lift music watch time by 25%.

Creator and Video Supply Growth

Daily active creators increased 10% year over year, while daily video submissions rose 36%, strengthening Bilibili’s content supply. Creators with more than 1,000 followers grew over 25%, those with more than 10,000 followers rose more than 20%, and average creator income increased 25%.

UpDream AI Tool Traction

Bilibili’s UpDream AI-native video creation platform has generated more than 5 billion minutes of watch time since its April launch. More than 1,000 videos created with the tool have each surpassed 1 million views, suggesting early demand for AI-assisted content production.

Stronger Community Engagement and Retention

Users generated nearly 20 billion interactions per month, up 7% year over year, while each active user followed an average of 95 creators, an increase of more than 10%. Official members grew 11% to 307 million, and 12-month retention remained close to 80%.

Community Events and Esports Achievement

Bilibili World and Bilibili Macro Link attracted 400,000 young people from more than 30 countries and regions, highlighting the platform’s cultural reach. Bilibili Gaming also won the S16 League of Legends World Championship, while daily active users reached a record on the day of the final.

Advertising Revenue Growth

Advertising revenue rose 20% year over year to RMB 3.1 billion despite macroeconomic pressure across industries. The number of advertisers spending on Bilibili increased 11%, while search advertising revenue grew more than 50%, pointing to stronger performance-based demand.

Growth Across Advertising Verticals

Home decoration advertising revenue grew 51% year over year, footwear and apparel increased about 40%, and education rose more than 29%. The five largest advertising categories were games, Internet services, digital products and home appliances, automotive, and e-commerce.

AI Advertising Momentum and Efficiency

AI-related advertising revenue nearly doubled, increasing about 95% year over year, while the conversion rate for performance-based ads rose more than 20%. Bilibili is also testing AI-generated video advertisements and AI agents designed to improve campaign placement and efficiency.

Game Pipeline and New-Title Progress

Lumi Master reached No. 2 on China’s iOS download chart following its September 17 global launch, with overseas markets contributing roughly 45% of gross revenue by the end of October. Sanwang is scheduled to launch on December 24, and management identified it and Ragnarok Online 3 as the company’s most important upcoming titles.

Robust 2027 Game Pipeline

Bilibili’s 2027 pipeline includes Ragnarok Online 3, Mistbound: Guild Wars and the self-developed Three Kingdoms: The Ravages of Time. All three titles have entered early testing and received positive or enthusiastic user feedback, with Mistbound targeted for release in the second half of 2027.

VAS and Premium Membership Growth

Value-added services revenue increased 4% year over year to RMB 3.1 billion, supported by continued membership expansion. Premium members reached 24.7 million at the end of the third quarter, about 80% of whom used annual subscriptions or automatic renewal, while fan charging revenue grew 40%.

Disciplined AI Investment Strategy

Management said AI spending would remain tightly focused on video consumption, community data use and creator tools. The company plans to continue investing in recommendations, creator products and computing infrastructure, but said the pace remains disciplined and well within its financial capacity.

Strong Cash Position and Share Repurchases

Cash, time deposits and short-term investments totaled RMB 25.71 billion as of September 30, 2026, giving Bilibili significant financial flexibility. The company repurchased and canceled USD 300 million of shares, reducing its share count by about 4.9%, while approximately USD 250.8 million remained available under a separate buyback program.

Game Revenue Decline

Game revenue fell 7% year over year to RMB 1.4 billion in the third quarter, making it one of the clearest weak points in the results. Management is relying on new releases and a deeper pipeline to restore growth after the current period of pressure.

Macro Pressure and Cautious Advertiser Budgets

Management said macroeconomic conditions and consumer sentiment remained challenging during the second half of the year. Advertisers became more selective, moving away from broad spending and placing greater emphasis on campaigns with predictable returns.

Expected Moderation in AI Advertising Growth

Bilibili expects the rapid growth of AI-related advertising budgets to moderate naturally as the comparison base becomes larger. Even so, management views AI as an important structural growth driver that should continue improving advertising efficiency and expanding monetization opportunities.

Higher Operating Expenses and R&D Investment

Total operating expenses increased 7% year over year to RMB 2.6 billion, while research and development costs rose 11%. The increase was driven mainly by continued investment in AI capabilities, creating some near-term pressure even as the company’s profitability improves.

Near-Term Margin Outlook

For the fourth quarter, management expects adjusted operating margin to remain in the high single digits. Gross profit margin is expected to be broadly flat from the previous quarter, suggesting that near-term profitability gains may be more measured than in the third quarter.

Conditional Nature of Some AI Investments

Some AI-related investments may be one-off, short term or dependent on the results of early experiments and testing. Management indicated that the financial impact in 2027 will depend largely on what the company learns from those initiatives and how successfully they translate into products and revenue.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management expects advertising to continue outgrowing the industry with healthy, steady growth in the fourth quarter and next year, although AI-related budget growth should moderate as the base expands. Full-year 2026 non-GAAP operating profit is expected to approach RMB 2.8 billion, up about 14% to 15%, while 2027 free cash flow is expected to exceed 2026; Lumi Master is expected to become profitable next year, and game revenue is expected to improve substantially in 2027.

Bilibili’s earnings call showed a platform with stronger engagement, healthier margins and growing advertising momentum, supported by an active creator ecosystem and early AI gains. Investors will nevertheless watch the game recovery, macro-sensitive advertising demand and the cost discipline surrounding AI as the company moves toward its next phase of growth.

data.title: Tongcheng Travel Earnings Call Highlights Growth Amid Headwinds
data.description:
Tongcheng Travel Holdings Limited ((HK:0780)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Tongcheng Travel Earnings Call Shows Growth Despite Market Headwinds

The earnings call struck a broadly positive tone, led by steady revenue and profit growth, strong international travel demand, expanding hotel management and record user engagement. Management also highlighted AI adoption and ample liquidity, although weaker transportation and tourism revenue, regulatory pressure, higher costs, competition and limited visibility for 2027 remained important risks.

Revenue and Profit Continue to Rise

Tongcheng Travel reported third-quarter revenue of RMB 5.8 billion, up 5.3% year over year. Adjusted net profit increased 6.7% to RMB 1.13 billion, lifting the adjusted margin to 19.5% from 19.2% a year earlier.

Core OTA Delivers Solid Results

Core online travel agency revenue rose 7.5% to RMB 5 billion in the quarter. Core OTA operating profit reached RMB 1.5 billion, producing a strong 30.4% operating margin.

Gross Profit and EBITDA Improve

Gross profit increased 9.7% to RMB 4 billion, while gross margin expanded to 68.5%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 4.9% to RMB 1.6 billion, showing continued operating resilience despite a tougher market.

Accommodation Business Remains Resilient

Accommodation reservation revenue rose 5.9% to RMB 1.7 billion, supported by higher average daily rates and room nights sold. Mid- to high-star hotels increased their share of platform supply by two percentage points year over year.

International Accommodation Sets Records

Average daily international room nights sold climbed more than 40% year over year to another record. International accommodation revenue now represents 5% of total accommodation reservation revenue, up from 3% last year.

International Air Ticketing Gains Momentum

Average daily international air ticket volume reached a record after rising more than 16% year over year. International air ticketing revenue accounted for 9.6% of transportation ticketing revenue, nearly four percentage points higher than a year earlier.

Hotel Management Network Expands Rapidly

Tongcheng’s hotel network approached 3,800 properties at the end of September, nearly 700 more than at the start of the year. Wanda Hotels and Resorts operated more than 330 hotels, resorts and commercial complexes, while Elong Hotel Technology managed nearly 3,500 hotels.

Hotel Management Becomes a Growth Engine

Hotel management revenue more than doubled and contributed over 40% of other revenue in the quarter. Elong Hotel Technology’s focus on mid-scale and upper mid-scale brands supported year-over-year growth in both average daily rate and revenue per available room.

International Hotel Supply Broadens

The company continued to add hotel supply and products across Southeast Asia and Northeast Asia. Wanda Hotels and Resorts also entered Africa for the first time this year, extending the group’s international reach.

Other Business Revenue Advances

Other business revenue grew 36.1% year over year to RMB 1.1 billion. The increase was mainly driven by the stronger performance of the hotel management business.

User Engagement and Monetization Strengthen

Standalone app daily active users exceeded 5.6 million ahead of the National Day holiday, setting a new record. Twelve-month average revenue per user surpassed RMB 82, an increase of nearly 11% year over year.

Large User Base Supports Scale

Tongcheng served more than 2 billion cumulative travelers during the 12 months ended September. Average paying users reached 250 million, implying that users made more than eight purchases on average during the period.

AI Adoption Gains Traction

DeepTrip had served nearly 20 million users since launch, with related order volumes continuing to grow. Tongcheng is integrating AI across trip planning, product discovery, bookings, customer service and internal operations.

AI Improves Service and Efficiency

AI-powered presale consultation for packaged tours improved efficiency and significantly raised order conversion. Flight assistants helped users search by budget and schedule, while AI customer-service tools identified pain points, improved issue resolution and reduced handling time.

Weixin AI Assistant Enters Testing

Tongcheng completed its initial integration with the Weixin AI Assistant and entered gray testing. The process is testing user-intent understanding, content retrieval and the complete booking process.

Liquidity Remains Strong

Cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments totaled RMB 15.7 billion as of September 30, 2026. The balance gives Tongcheng financial flexibility as it invests in growth, pursues strategic opportunities and manages market volatility.

Investigation Has Not Disrupted Operations

Management said it is fully cooperating with an ongoing regulatory investigation involving the company and several OTA platforms. It added that daily business operations remained normal, with no material disruption observed.

Shareholder Returns Under Review

Management said it aims to further enhance shareholder returns this year, subject to board approval. It also emphasized a balanced approach covering business investment, strategic mergers and acquisitions, and returns to shareholders.

Travel Market Faces Persistent Headwinds

China’s travel market continued to face pressure from extreme weather, geopolitical uncertainty, cautious consumer spending and unclear fuel costs. Management described overall industry growth as modest and said travel demand remained under pressure.

Transportation Revenue Declines

Transportation ticketing revenue fell 2% year over year to RMB 2.2 billion. Frequent extreme weather weakened demand, while regulatory adjustments also affected the train-ticketing business.

Tourism Revenue Comes Under Pressure

Tourism revenue declined 6% to RMB 845.9 million. Outbound packaged tours remained affected by geopolitical uncertainty and rising fuel costs, which weighed on consumer demand.

Train Ticketing Faces Regulatory Pressure

Management expects train-ticketing regulation to continue affecting revenue and profitability. The segment’s contribution to OTA revenue has fallen from about 35% in 2018 to roughly 15% to 16% in the third quarter of 2026.

Higher Fuel Costs Weigh on Demand

Aviation fuel surcharges were raised twice in October and November, reaching RMB 80 for domestic routes of 800 kilometers or less and RMB 140 for longer routes. Management said the increases put further pressure on fares, air-ticketing demand and outbound travel.

APU Falls for the First Time

Average paying users declined for the first time in the third quarter. Softer travel demand, higher fuel surcharges, extreme weather and lower train-ticketing volumes all weighed on travel frequency and the paying-user base.

Operating and Marketing Costs Rise

Service development and administrative expenses increased 11% year over year as new businesses added headcount. Excluding share-based compensation, these costs rose to 15% of revenue from 13.8%, while selling and marketing expenses climbed 12.7% and reached 33.3% of revenue.

Transportation Take Rates Face Pressure

Management expects domestic air-ticketing take rates to decline slightly as higher fares reduce demand for value-added services. Train-ticketing volume and take rates are also expected to weaken because of changes in the operating environment.

Other Business Growth May Moderate

Other business revenue growth is expected to slow after three strong quarters, partly because the comparison base now includes Wanda Hotels and Resorts. Advertising growth may also moderate as market conditions soften.

Domestic OTA Competition Intensifies

Management acknowledged a changing competitive landscape, with more internet platforms using existing user traffic and content capabilities to enter travel services. Accommodation is a particular focus of this expanding competition.

Regulatory Review Remains Ongoing

The investigation involving several OTA platforms, including Tongcheng, is continuing. Management declined to discuss specific details but said it would keep reviewing platform policies, business practices and internal compliance measures.

Fourth-Quarter Outlook

Accommodation performance is expected to remain broadly in line with the third quarter, supported by room nights and average daily rates, while its take rate should remain stable. International air ticketing is expected to deliver strong volume and revenue growth, but train ticketing is likely to decline and other business growth should moderate.

Longer-Term Growth Priorities

Management expects hotel management to maintain strong revenue growth and improve profitability, while outbound products could represent about 9% of accommodation and transportation by the end of 2026. It said visibility into the 2027 operating environment remains limited.

Tongcheng Travel’s earnings call showed a company still delivering growth through core OTA services, international travel, hotel management and AI. However, weaker domestic transportation demand, regulation, rising costs and competition could limit near-term momentum, making execution and disciplined investment central to the stock’s outlook.

data.title: Deere Earnings Call Highlights Growth Amid 2027 Risks
data.description:
Deere & Company ((DE)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Deere & Company’s fiscal 2026 earnings call carried a broadly positive tone, supported by strong full-year profitability, disciplined inventories, growth in Small Ag & Turf and Construction & Forestry, and rising technology adoption. However, weak Large Ag conditions, soft overseas markets, tariffs, cost pressures and potential labor disruption kept management’s outlook measured.

Strong Fiscal 2026 Profitability

Deere reported fiscal 2026 net sales and revenues of $47.7 billion, up 4%, while Equipment Operations sales rose 6% to $41.3 billion. Net income attributable to Deere reached $4.86 billion, or $17.95 per diluted share, and the full-year Equipment Operations margin was 12.2%.

Fourth-Quarter Execution

The company ended the year with a 9.3% Equipment Operations margin and fourth-quarter net income of $1.05 billion, or $3.89 per diluted share. All operating segments were in line with or ahead of the guidance issued in the previous quarter.

Structural Margin Improvement

Equipment Operations produced margins above 12% even though Production & Precision Ag remained below trough-cycle levels. Deere said its comparable margin profile was more than 400 basis points higher than in 2016, reflecting better cost control, tighter inventories and a larger technology mix.

Small Ag & Turf Growth

Small Ag & Turf fourth-quarter sales increased 10% to $2.7 billion, driven by higher shipments and favorable pricing, while full-year sales rose about 15%. The segment posted a 15.1% operating margin, and its tractor business in India recorded a fiscal-year sales record.

Construction & Forestry Expansion

Construction & Forestry fourth-quarter sales rose 12% to $3.8 billion, helped by higher volumes and pricing, while full-year sales climbed nearly 22%. Infrastructure, non-residential construction, rental fleet replacement and rental fleet growth supported results that slightly exceeded the company’s annual outlook.

Inventory Discipline

New North American Large Ag equipment inventories remained tight, falling 10% from already low year-earlier levels. Used high-horsepower tractor inventories were down 25% from their peak, used combines declined about 30%, and model-year 2023 and 2024 tractor inventories fell more than 40% year over year.

Large Ag Demand Indicators Improve

North American Early Order Programs were running up double digits, with especially strong planter demand and combine orders also up double digits. Large-tractor backlog momentum improved steadily, with orders in hand extending through the middle of the second quarter.

Precision Ag Adoption Accelerates

Engaged Acres surpassed 530 million globally, Highly Engaged Acres exceeded 200 million, and monthly active digital users grew nearly 25% to more than 500,000. Connected equipment topped 1.2 million machines, while See & Spray covered about 12 million acres and generated average herbicide savings above 50%.

Customer Productivity Gains

See & Spray utilization in the U.S. and Canada increased about 30%, and roughly one-third of recent sprayer orders included the technology. Harvest Settings Automation was used across 11 million combine acres, while Predictive Ground Speed Automation delivered about 20% greater productivity with lower fuel use.

Construction Technology Growth

Sales of grade management, job-site safety and automation solutions grew about 30% in 2026. More than 90% of orders for Deere’s new 20-metric-ton excavators included grade control, while fleet-management solutions were tracking ahead of expectations.

JD AI Assistant Launch

Deere introduced JD, an artificial-intelligence assistant that uses customer operations data to support equipment users. During its first week of full availability, more than 6,000 users in 76 countries held over 10,000 conversations with the service.

Investment in Future Growth

Deere is continuing to invest in customer solutions, factory automation, efficient production and digital platforms. Planned initiatives include Small Ag & Turf applications, excavator development, the Tenna construction platform, Orchard AI and other targeted acquisitions.

Cash Generation and Shareholder Returns

Management projected fiscal 2027 net operating cash flow of $4.5 billion to $5.5 billion. Deere said its priorities remain preserving an A credit rating, funding growth and returning excess cash through dividends and share repurchases.

Cost Control and Pricing

The company reported productivity gains across operations and supplies and said pricing actions are designed to offset expected inflation. Deere is also working with suppliers on sourcing and design changes intended to reduce costs without compromising product quality.

Brazil Technology Opportunity

Brazilian customers ordered factory-installed See & Spray for the first time, with initial adoption running at roughly twice North America’s first-year rate. Deere is also installing JDLink Boost on every Large Ag machine leaving its factories, supporting longer-term digital adoption.

Fourth-Quarter Consolidated Declines

Despite solid full-year performance, fourth-quarter net sales and revenues fell 2% to $12.1 billion, while Equipment Operations sales declined 1% to $10.5 billion. Net income attributable to Deere decreased 1% to $1.05 billion.

Production & Precision Ag Weakness

Production & Precision Ag fourth-quarter sales dropped 15% to $4 billion, mainly because of lower shipments, while operating profit fell to $406 million. Full-year sales declined about 9% across North America, South America and Europe, although lower production costs and currency effects provided some offset.

Tight Farm Economics

Large Ag customers continue to face narrow farm margins, high input costs and volatile commodity markets. Deere said crop prices have retreated from recent highs, conditions that are likely to slow the pace of industry recovery.

Regional Agriculture Challenges

Europe faces pressure from weaker crop yields, elevated input costs and tighter lending conditions, while South America remains constrained by high interest rates, currency volatility and uncertain weather. These factors are delaying purchases and keeping regional equipment volumes near historically low levels.

Small Ag & Turf Market Constraints

Small Ag & Turf industry sales in the U.S. and Canada are expected to remain roughly flat as high mortgage rates and a soft housing market limit turf-equipment demand. Europe is also facing some downward market pressure.

Construction Margin Pressure

Construction & Forestry’s fourth-quarter operating profit slipped slightly to $339 million, producing an 8.9% margin. Higher production, selling, administrative and research costs outweighed favorable pricing, while weak residential construction, forestry markets and possible data-center spending risks remain concerns.

Financial Services Decline

Worldwide Financial Services fourth-quarter net income fell to $231 million. The decline reflected weaker financing spreads, a smaller average portfolio and a higher provision for credit losses.

Fiscal 2027 Profit Range

Deere expects fiscal 2027 net income of $4.5 billion to $5.25 billion, a range below or near the prior year’s result. The forecast includes about $500 million of higher pension-related impacts, including a potential one-time, tax-adjusted non-cash settlement charge of $250 million to $400 million.

Tariff Headwinds

Direct tariff costs exceeded $1.1 billion in 2026 before refunds, and Deere expects the 2027 run rate to ease slightly to about $1 billion. Because last year’s refunds will not repeat, the company anticipates a roughly $300 million net headwind.

Raw Material and Freight Costs

Steel, other raw materials and freight remain on an upward trend. Deere said these costs are incorporated into its outlook and should be addressed through pricing actions and procurement efforts.

UAW Contract Risk

Deere’s labor agreements with the UAW expire at the end of fiscal 2027, and the company is preparing for several possible outcomes, including a work stoppage. Such actions could create a notable increase in working capital needs, particularly in the fourth quarter.

2027 Margin Investment

Growth investments, tariffs and other pressures are expected to weigh on Small Ag & Turf and Construction & Forestry margins in 2027. At the midpoint, Small Ag & Turf’s margin is about two points lower, with roughly half the reduction tied to tariffs and half to investment.

Soft Forestry and Housing Markets

Global forestry markets are expected to remain roughly flat as weak housing activity limits improvement. Elevated mortgage rates continue to weigh on residential construction and smaller and mid-sized contractors.

Fiscal 2027 Guidance

Deere expects Production & Precision Ag sales to rise 5% to 15%, with a 12.5% to 14.5% margin, while Small Ag & Turf sales should be roughly flat with a 12.5% to 13.5% margin. Construction & Forestry sales are forecast to range from flat to up 10%, with a 9.5% to 11.5% margin, and Financial Services income is expected to reach $900 million.

The company also projects a 23% to 25% effective tax rate, net income of $4.5 billion to $5.25 billion and operating cash flow of $4.5 billion to $5.5 billion. Management expects pricing, procurement and productivity actions to help offset tariffs, inflation and currency pressure, but pension costs and labor uncertainty remain important risks.

Deere’s call showed a business with stronger structural margins, healthy technology adoption and encouraging order signals in North American Large Ag and construction. Still, subdued farm economics, regional weakness and several cost and execution risks suggest that fiscal 2027 will be a year of measured recovery rather than a broad-based rebound.

data.title: GDS Holdings Earnings Call Signals AI-Driven Growth
data.description:
GDS Holdings ((GDS)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

GDS Holdings delivered a predominantly positive message on its earnings call, pointing to strong AI infrastructure demand, solid bookings and high-quality customers in China. Management also highlighted stable data-center economics, improving utilization and clear visibility into future billings and EBITDA, while acknowledging near-term utilization pressure, legacy contract repricing and higher planned net debt.

AI Demand Drives China Focus

GDS said it remains fully focused on providing data-center services in China, where artificial intelligence is developing rapidly. Management described demand for AI infrastructure as robust, supporting the company’s growth plans.

Bookings Maintain Strong Momentum

Bookings reached 686 megawatts in the first nine months of 2026. GDS expects to reach its full-year target of about 1 gigawatt, while its backlog model uses an assumption of 950 megawatts in new bookings.

Leading Internet Customers Anchor Growth

More than 80% of new business is coming from China’s three largest Internet and cloud customers. GDS described these clients as high quality and noted that it has served them for many years.

Selective, Contracted Expansion

GDS said it remains selective when adding new business and favors orders based on domestic technologies. Take-or-pay contracts, with customer move-in periods averaging 12 months, provide support for the disclosed bookings.

Projects Have Strong Delivery Support

New projects are located in national hubs with available land and power, backed by local and central government support. Management said approvals are based on proven demand and financing capacity, while supply-chain bottlenecks are not currently an issue.

Data-Center Economics Remain Stable

Management reported stable pricing, development costs and project yields. Current pricing, it said, continues to support reasonable risk-adjusted returns despite a competitive and rapidly changing market.

Bookings Are Fully Funded

GDS said its roughly 1 gigawatt of expected bookings for 2026 is fully funded by existing financial resources. The company also has access to low-cost domestic bank debt and domestic equity markets through its asset-monetization strategy.

Shanghai C-REIT Platform Advances

GDS has established one of only two data-center REITs listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. It is at an advanced stage of seeking approval for its first post-IPO asset injection, which it expects to complete early next year.

Backlog Visibility Continues to Improve

The company began 2026 with a 450-megawatt backlog. Assuming 950 megawatts of new bookings and 250 megawatts of billings during the year, GDS expects its year-end backlog to reach 1.15 gigawatts.

Billings Could Exceed 2.4 Gigawatts

GDS expects total billings to reach 1.4 gigawatts by the end of 2026. After construction and ramp-up, the 1.15-gigawatt backlog is expected to become fully billable within two years, supporting billings above 2.4 gigawatts by the end of 2028, before additional new business.

Contracted EBITDA Points Higher

Annualized adjusted EBITDA is expected to reach about RMB 5.5 billion in the fourth quarter of 2026. After factoring in churn, asset monetization and price resets, GDS projects RMB 6.7 billion in the fourth quarter of 2028, a 21% increase that excludes new business after 2026.

Third-Quarter Growth Remained Positive

On a pro forma basis, third-quarter revenue rose 11.9% year over year, while adjusted EBITDA increased 6.2%. Management said the company remains on track to meet its revised 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA targets.

CapEx Timing Changes, Not Project Plans

GDS reduced full-year CapEx guidance to RMB 8.5 billion from RMB 10 billion because of a small shift in supplier payment timing. CapEx incurred during 2026 is expected to total about RMB 12 billion, with management emphasizing that project execution remains unchanged.

Funding Plan Supports Backlog Delivery

GDS expects to end 2026 with RMB 32 billion of net debt and plans to spend RMB 16 billion over the following two years to complete capacity tied to its year-end backlog. Management said the company is fully funded for delivery and expects net debt of about RMB 38 billion by the end of 2028.

Liquidity and Financing Remain Substantial

Cash resources stood at about RMB 19 billion, while operating cash flow reached RMB 2 billion in the first nine months excluding one-time items. GDS finances new investment with roughly 60% debt and 40% equity, using project loans, cash flow and asset-monetization proceeds.

Utilization Has Room to Recover

Management said utilization is currently at its highest level ever. However, as newly committed capacity enters service, utilization is expected to temporarily fall back into the 70s before recovering and trending toward the mid- to high 80s.

Move-In Assumptions Hold Steady

Customer contracts continue to allow move-in over an average period of 12 months. GDS said there has been no change to its assumptions about customer move-in cadence or the pace of ramp-up.

Domestic Technology Supports Supply Confidence

All current bookings rely on domestic technologies, according to management. GDS said it remains confident that its supply chain has no bottlenecks and that external volatility has not changed its delivery schedule or backlog assumptions.

2026 Revenue and EBITDA Targets Unchanged

GDS maintained its full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance. The decision reflects management’s continued confidence in operating performance despite a temporary utilization dip and slower adjusted EBITDA growth than revenue growth.

Revenue Growth Outpaced EBITDA

The third-quarter figures showed a difference in growth rates, with pro forma revenue up 11.9% and adjusted EBITDA up 6.2% year over year. The gap reflects near-term operating pressures as the company expands capacity and continues to manage pricing changes.

Net Debt Will Rise With Investment

Net debt stood at 5.1 times last-quarter annualized adjusted EBITDA at the end of the third quarter. GDS expects leverage to increase as it funds backlog delivery, rising from RMB 32 billion at the end of 2026 to about RMB 38 billion in 2028.

Legacy Contract Repricing Nears Completion

GDS remains in the final phase of repricing legacy contracts as they renew. Management expects the process to be largely completed within the next 18 months, which should clarify the effect of older agreements on future economics.

Convertible Bond Reserve Set Aside

The company has reserved RMB 4 billion in preparation for the early redemption of a convertible bond next year. The reserve is part of GDS’s broader liquidity and capital-management planning.

Guidance Points to Expanding Backlog and EBITDA

GDS expects about 1 gigawatt of 2026 bookings, a 1.15-gigawatt year-end backlog and 1.4 gigawatts of total billings. It projects billings above 2.4 gigawatts by the end of 2028, annualized adjusted EBITDA of RMB 5.5 billion in the fourth quarter of 2026 and RMB 6.7 billion in the fourth quarter of 2028, while utilization may briefly return to the 70s before reaching the mid- to high 80s.

Overall, GDS presented a confident outlook built on AI demand, contracted growth and a large, increasingly visible backlog. The main risks are the temporary utilization decline, slower EBITDA growth, legacy repricing and higher leverage, but management maintained its 2026 targets and said funding for planned expansion is in place.
